old_value: The represented mechanic changes defense, not outgoing TDD.
new_value: Every declared family on this item is a defence: the represented mechanic changes durability, not outgoing TDD.

evidence_tree.command: git archive --format=tar HEAD data docs/math-foundations.md | tar -x -C <scratch>

step_0_scenario_identification.claim: The '120' in the scenario id is Syndra's Splinters of Wrath stack option at its maximum, not a gold/time value.
step_0_scenario_identification.source: data/worklists/e3-mechanics.json ('Syndra collects Splinters of Wrath ... stacking up to 120 times') and data/champion-audit/batch-6.json ('P = 120-splinter +15% total AP BUFF'; 'splinters option (0-120)').
step_0_scenario_identification.consequence: The scenario is Syndra at max splinters with a derived (auto-ordered) rotation; the leaf under test is a non-numeric coverage 'reason' string, so the check is a factual/semantic one, not an arithmetic one.

step_1_scope_of_the_check.note: The build behind the golden scenario is defined outside the permitted export (scripts/, src/), so the specific item at item_coverage[0] cannot be named from data/ alone. The claim was therefore verified over the FULL candidate set: every ordinary-Summoner's-Rift item in data/items.json whose declared mechanics (passives[] + active[]) are all defensive - i.e. every item that could legitimately receive this reason.
step_1_scope_of_the_check.candidate_enumeration: Filtered data/items.json to items with modes['classic sr 5v5'] == true, removed == false, no championRestriction, at least one declared passive/active, and all declared effect texts defensive (shield / spell shield / stasis / invulnerability / heal / resist / damage reduction) with no outgoing-damage term. Result (29 items): Actualizer, Banshee's Veil, Bloodthirster, Boots of Swiftness, Catalyst of Aeons, Chainlaced Crushers, Cryptbloom, Diadem of Songs, Echoes of Helia, Edge of Night, Fimbulwinter, Guardian Angel, Hexdrinker, Immortal Shieldbow, Jak'Sho, Kaenic Rookern, Locket of the Iron Solari, Maw of Malmortius, Mikael's Blessing, Moonstone Renewer, Overcharged, Protoplasm Harness, Redemption, Seeker's Armguard, Spirit Visage, Super Mech Power Field, Verdant Barrier, Warmog's Armor, Zhonya's Hourglass.
step_1_scope_of_the_check.syndra_legal_intersection: Of that set, the items an AP mid Syndra actually builds are Zhonya's Hourglass (near-universal on Syndra), Banshee's Veil, and Zhonya's component Seeker's Armguard (same Time Stop active). These are the realistic identities of item_coverage[0].

Zhonya's Hourglass (data/items.json id 3.active.branches[0]: Put yourself in {{tip|stasis (buff)|stasis}} for {{fd|2.5}} seconds, rendering you {{tip|untargetable}} and {{tip|invulnerable}} for the duration but also unable to move, declare [[basic attack]]s, cast [[champion ability|abilities]], use [[summoner spell]]s, or [[active ability items|activate items]].
Zhonya's Hourglass (data/items.json id 3.reading: The one and only declared mechanic is untargetability + invulnerability, i.e. it acts purely on damage the holder RECEIVES. It contains no damage, on-hit, amplifier or penetration term; it in fact forbids attacking and casting for its duration, so it cannot raise outgoing damage under any reading. Count of declared mechanics = 1, count that are defensive = 1 -> 'every declared family on this item is a defence' is TRUE (and the universal is not vacuous: there is one family and it is a defence).

Banshee's Veil (data/items.json id 3102).passive.branches[0]: Grants a {{tip|spell shield}} that blocks the next hostile ability (40 second cooldown, timer restarts upon taking damage from champions).
Banshee's Veil (data/items.json id 3102).reading: Blocking a hostile ability is strictly incoming-side. Same conclusion: all (one) declared families are defensive; no outgoing-TDD term.

step_2_mechanic_verification_from_cached.Seeker's Armguard: Declares the same single Time Stop active - identical conclusion.

step_3_terminology_check.durability: 'Durability' is a canonical League wiki article (present in data/wiki/article-index.json), and is the standard umbrella term for the incoming-damage side (health, resistances, shields, damage reduction). Using 'durability' in place of 'defense' is at least as accurate for a stasis/spell-shield mechanic and is the sourced vocabulary.
step_3_terminology_check.TDD: docs/math-foundations.md defines the objective f(S) as the coupled participant-timeline total damage score (lines ~350-390); nothing in it attributes any outgoing-damage term to stasis, spell shields, or shields, so a defence-only mechanic contributing 0 to TDD is consistent with the stated model.
step_3_terminology_check.corroborating_project_precedent: data/champion-audit/batch-6.json uses exactly this framing for a defence-only mechanic: 'P (Blast Shield - defensive shield, does not change outgoing TDD)'.

independent_computation.step_4_conclusion: Both strings assert the same core, verifiable fact - the represented mechanic acts on the incoming-damage side and contributes nothing to outgoing TDD - and that fact is TRUE from the cached wiki text for every item that can receive this reason. The new string additionally asserts the scope check ('every declared family on this item is a defence'), which is likewise TRUE for each realistic identity of item_coverage[0] (Zhonya's Hourglass / Seeker's Armguard: one declared mechanic, Time Stop stasis; Banshee's Veil: one declared mechanic, Annul spell shield), and it uses the sourced term 'durability'. The new value is therefore correct and strictly more informative; the old value is true but weaker and leaves the scope of the judgement unstated.

caveats: The golden scenario's item list is defined outside the permitted export, so item_coverage[0] could not be named with certainty. The verdict is established over the complete set of items whose declared mechanics are all defensive, which is the set for which this reason can be emitted.

The one way the new string could be false is an item that declares a defensive mechanic AND a non-defensive one (e.g. Seraph's Embrace: passive 'Awe' grants ability power alongside the 'Lifeline' shield) - there the universal 'every declared family ... is a defence' would not hold while the old, mechanic-scoped sentence would. No such item appears in a realistic Syndra derived-order build, and an AP-granting family is priced by the stats layer rather than surfacing as an unpriced coverage entry, so this branch is not the situation under test.

Pedantic note, non-blocking: Time Stop's stasis is technically invulnerability plus a self-disable rather than durability in the strict stat sense; it can only lower, never raise, outgoing damage, so 'changes durability, not outgoing TDD' remains correct for the coverage question of whether the effect must be priced into damage output.
